notes.meaning: Paul speaks about the return of the Lord Jesus Christ and the gathering of all believers to be with Him. This gathering will bring all of God's people together into complete joy and safety in Christ's presence forever. Knowing that believers will be kept safe with Christ should take away fear of the judgment day.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe Christ's return has two separate stages, first coming for the church in a secret rapture and later coming with the church to judge the world.

notes.meaning: Paul urges the believers not to be alarmed or unsettled in their thinking by rumors that the Day of the Lord has already arrived. People were spreading this false claim through fake revelations, misquoted teachings, or forged letters claiming to be from the apostles. Believers must not let sudden fears shake their confidence in God's truth.

Paul warns that no one should trick them, because Christ will not return until two major events happen first. There must first be a widespread religious rebellion against God, followed by the appearance of a terribly wicked leader called the man of lawlessness. This shows that the end was not happening immediately in their day.

This wicked leader will openly oppose God and put himself above everything that people worship. He will even take his seat in God's temple and claim divine authority and honor for himself. His proud goal is to push aside God's commands and demand that people honor him instead.

differ.view: Reformed Christians have historically seen this passage fulfilled in the office of the papacy ruling inside the visible church.
Lutherans historically taught that the papacy was the seat of the true Antichrist.
Many evangelicals believe this refers to a single future ruler who will set himself up in a rebuilt temple in Jerusalem.

notes.meaning: Paul gently asks the believers if they remember his earlier visits. He had already taught them these truths in person while living and ministering among them. This reminded them that they had no good reason to be surprised or panicked by false rumors.

Paul explains that a restraining power is currently holding back this evil until God's appointed time for it to be shown. Secret rebellion is already quietly at work behind the scenes, but it cannot fully break out until the one who restrains is taken out of the way. God remains in complete control over history and keeps evil within set bounds.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe the restrainer is the Holy Spirit who will be removed along with the church before the Great Tribulation.
Reformed Christians have often identified the restraining power as civil rulers and lawful government, such as the Roman empire.

notes.meaning: Once the restraining power is removed, the lawless leader will step out into open view. Yet his power will not last, because the Lord Jesus will destroy him simply by the breath of His mouth and the glorious arrival of His coming. Christ's victory over this great enemy will be complete, effortless, and final.

The arrival of the lawless ruler is empowered by Satan through counterfeit miracles, signs, and lying wonders. He will use every kind of evil trickery to fool those who are headed for ruin. These people perish because they deliberately chose not to love and welcome the truth that could have saved them.

Because these people rejected the truth, God allows a powerful delusion to take hold of their minds so that they believe what is false. This is God's fair judgment on those who refused His word. Everyone who preferred sin and took pleasure in wickedness instead of trusting God's truth will face righteous condemnation.

Paul offers heartfelt thanks to God for these believers whom the Lord dearly loves. God chose them from the beginning for salvation, setting them apart to be made holy by the Holy Spirit and through their trust in the gospel truth. God's choice brings deep comfort and safety to those who follow Him.

differ.view: Reformed Christians believe God chose specific individuals for salvation from before the creation of the world, producing both faith and holiness in them.
Methodists understand God choosing believers from the beginning of their hearing the gospel, with final glory depending on their continued faithfulness.

notes.meaning: God invited believers to this salvation through the preaching of the good news of Jesus. The purpose of this calling is that Christians will one day share in the magnificent glory of the Lord Jesus Christ Himself. Believers can be sure that God's plan leads to their final honor with Christ.

In light of God's great love and call, believers are told to stand firm and hold tightly to the teachings they were given. Paul had passed down these truths both by his spoken words and by his written letters. Christians are called to guard the pure apostolic message without adding human ideas to it.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics teach that this verse supports the authority of Sacred Tradition alongside written Scripture as an equal channel of apostolic teaching.

notes.meaning: Paul prays directly to the Lord Jesus Christ and God the Father, who showed believers unearned favor and gave them lasting comfort and good hope. He asks God to strengthen their hearts and help them remain steadfast in everything they say and do. True comfort from God gives believers the power to lead holy and useful lives.
